1. "openspec instructions apply --change add-xtb-optimization --json" reports zero remaining required implementation tasks.

2. Every explicit requirement and scenario in the active OpenSpec change has corresponding implementation evidence.

3. OpenSpec task completion accurately reflects the actual codebase state; no checkbox is marked complete merely because work was attempted.

4. Relevant builds, tests, and regression checks pass.

5. No known required work, implementation blocker, knowingly failing relevant test, or silently deferred required task remains.

6. A final comparison of the OpenSpec artifacts against the resulting implementation finds no substantive omission.

7. The repository is left in a coherent state suitable for subsequent OpenSpec verification/archive work.

8. Every mirrored GLLA task is complete (the GLLA task list shows no open tasks), so GLLA's pending-task gate does not refuse completion.

Do not declare the GLLA goal complete based only on previous conversation claims or task checkboxes. Verify against current repository and OpenSpec evidence.

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1] 1.1 Vendor the xTB API header. Create directory `libavogadro/src/xtb/`. Copy the xTB C API header into `libavogadro/src/xtb/xtb.h` — take it verbatim from the Ubuntu package `libxtb-dev` 6.6.1 (`/usr/include/xtb.h`; if not installed: `cd /tmp && apt-get download libxtb-dev && dpkg -x libxtb-dev*.deb ext/ && cp ext/usr/include/xtb.h libavogadro/src/xtb/xtb.h`). Also create `libavogadro/src/xtb/README.md` with three lines: source package+version, upstream project (grimme-lab/xtb), and "header only — the library itself is resolved at runtime, never linked". Do not modify anything else in the header. — Verify: `echo '#include "xtb.h"' > /tmp/hdrcheck.cpp` compiles with `-I libavogadro/src/xtb -fsyntax-only` using g++: `g++ -std=c++17 -I libavogadro/src/xtb -fsyntax-only /tmp/hdrcheck.cpp` exits 0.

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Create the runtime loader `libavogadro/src/xtb/xtbapi.h` + `libavogadro/src/xtb/xtbapi.cpp`, class `Avogadro::XtbApi` (all-static public API, no instances): `static bool isAvailable();` (loads once, caches), `static QString lastError();`, and one static accessor per C function, returning a function pointer or `nullptr` when unavailable. Include `"xtb.h"` from the same directory and declare typedefs for every function pointer used: `xtb_newEnvironment`, `xtb_delEnvironment`, `xtb_checkEnvironment`, `xtb_getError`, `xtb_setVerbosity`, `xtb_newMolecule`, `xtb_delMolecule`, `xtb_updateMolecule`, `xtb_newCalculator`, `xtb_delCalculator`, `xtb_loadGFN0xTB`, `xtb_loadGFN1xTB`, `xtb_loadGFN2xTB`, `xtb_loadGFNFF`, `xtb_setAccuracy`, `xtb_setMaxIter`, `xtb_setElectronicTemp`, `xtb_singlepoint`, `xtb_newResults`, `xtb_delResults`, `xtb_getEnergy`, `xtb_getGradient`. Loading: `QLibrary` tried in order `libxtb-6` (Windows), `libxtb.so.6`, `libxtb.so` (non-Windows); resolve via `QLibrary::resolve`; on total failure set the error string naming the tried names and return false from `isAvailable()`. Thread-safety: guard the one-time load with a `QMutex` (static). No MOC needed (no `Q_OBJECT`). — Verify: `cmake --build build --target avogadro -j8` succeeds after 1.3 registers the files.

[OpenSpec 3] 1.3 Register the shim in the library build. In `libavogadro/src/CMakeLists.txt` add `xtb/xtbapi.cpp` to `libavogadro_SRCS` (or the equivalent sources list used there) and `xtb/xtbapi.h` + `xtb/xtb.h` to the headers list, following how existing subdirectory sources are added in that file. Do not add any find/link of xTB. — Verify: `cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build --target avogadro -j8` succeeds, and `nm -D build/libavogadro/libavogadro.so* 2>/dev/null | grep -c XtbApi` is > 0 (symbols exported), and the configure log contains NO new xTB-related find output.

[OpenSpec 4] 1.4 New test `libavogadro/tests/xtbruntimetest.cpp` + target. Test class `XtbRuntimeTest`, two slots: `absentIsHarmless` — if `XtbApi::isAvailable()` is false, assert `lastError()` is non-empty and return (QSKIP is also acceptable); if true, QSKIP with "library present" (this slot only checks the absent path); `waterGfn2Singlepoint` — QSKIP when `!XtbApi::isAvailable()`; otherwise build a water molecule through the function pointers (O + 2 H exactly as in the existing `libavogadro/tests/xtbphysicstest.cpp` coordinates), run `loadGFN2xTB` + `singlepoint` + `getEnergy`, `QVERIFY(energy < 0.0)`, and free all four objects in order (results, calculator, molecule, environment). Add `xtbruntime` to the `tests` list in `libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt` (the plain list near the top, NOT inside any `if(XTB_FOUND)` block) — the target builds with no xTB linkage. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target xtbruntimetest -j8 && xvfb-run ctest -R xtbruntimetest --output-on-failure` passes (on this machine the library may be absent → skips; on the CI `xtb=ON` leg it runs).

[OpenSpec 5] 1.5 Rewrite `libavogadro/tests/xtbphysicstest.cpp` onto the shim. Replace `#include <xtb.h>` with `#include "xtb/xtbapi.h"` (adjust include path per how tests include library headers — follow the pattern of the includes already at the top of `xtbphysicstest.cpp`), route every xTB call through the `XtbApi` function pointers, add `if (!XtbApi::isAvailable()) QSKIP("xTB runtime library not available");` as the first line of `energy()`, and delete the energy/gradient call differences only as needed — the test keeps its single `energy()` slot asserting `energy < 0.0` for water GFN2. In `libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt` remove `xtbphysics` from the `if(XTB_FOUND) list(APPEND tests ...)` line (leave `xtbopttool` there — it is removed later in task 6.1) and add `xtbphysics` to the plain `tests` list; delete the now-dead lines `target_link_libraries(xtbphysicstest PRIVATE ${XTB_LIBRARIES})` and the matching OpenMP line for `xtbphysicstest` only (keep `xtbopttooltest`'s lines — still needed until task 6.1). — Verify: `cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build --target xtbphysicstest -j8 && xvfb-run ctest -R xtbphysicstest --output-on-failure` passes, and `grep -c "XTB_LIBRARIES" libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt` shows only `xtbopttooltest` occurrences remain.

[OpenSpec 6] 2.1 Create `libavogadro/src/xtb/lbfgs.h` + `libavogadro/src/xtb/lbfgs.cpp`, namespace `Avogadro::Xtb`, class `LBfgs`. Public surface (fixed by design D5 — implement exactly this): constructor takes nothing; `void setHistory(int m)` (default constant `kLBfgsHistory = 10`); `struct Result { bool converged; int evaluations; double finalGradNorm; };`; `template <typename Eval, typename Stop> Result minimize(std::vector<double>& coords, Eval&& evaluate, Stop&& shouldStop)` — `evaluate` has signature `double(const std::vector<double>& coords, std::vector<double>& grad)` returning energy and filling the gradient of equal length; `shouldStop` has signature `bool(int evaluations)` returning true when the caller wants to stop (cancelled/max cap). Also `void resetHistory()`. Implementation: standard two-loop recursion L-BFGS with a backtracking Armijo line search (initial step 1.0, shrink factor 0.5, `c1 = 1e-4`, at most 20 shrink steps per iteration; fall back to a small fixed step `1e-3` scaled by inverse gradient norm if Armijo never accepts — never loop forever); convergence is caller-declared: add `double gradNorm(const std::vector<double>&) const` helper and let the CALLER compare against thresholds (the engine owns thresholds per D5). All plain `std::vector`/`<cmath>` — no Qt, no Eigen, no xTB includes. MSVC-safe. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target avogadro -j8` after 2.3 registers the file.

[OpenSpec 7] 2.2 New test `libavogadro/tests/lbfgstest.cpp` + target `lbfgstest` (add `lbfgs` to the plain `tests` list in `libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt` — no library linkage beyond the avogadro lib). Four slots: `quadraticConverges` (2-atom flat system: f = sum((x-3)^2), grad = 2(x-3), assert final grad norm < 1e-6 within 100 evaluations), `rosenbrockConverges` (2-variable Rosenbrock a=1 b=100 from (-1.2, 1.0), assert |x-1| < 1e-2 within 1000 evaluations), `maxEvaluationsStops` (same Rosenbrock but `shouldStop` returns true at 10 evaluations; assert `Result::evaluations <= 11` and no crash), `historyResetWorks` (run to partial convergence, call `resetHistory()`, run again, assert convergence still reached). — Verify: `cmake --build build --target lbfgstest -j8 && xvfb-run ctest -R lbfgstest --output-on-failure` green.

[OpenSpec 8] 3.1 Engine skeleton + setup lifecycle. Create `libavogadro/src/xtb/xtbengine.h` + `libavogadro/src/xtb/xtbengine.cpp`, class `Avogadro::XtbEngine : public QThread` (follow the structure of `AutoOptThread` in `libavogadro/src/tools/autoopttool.h` — constructor/destructor, `setup(...)`, `run()`, `stop()`, signals). Public surface (fixed — implement exactly this): `bool setup(const std::vector<int>& atomicNumbers, const std::vector<double>& positionsAngstrom, int method /* 0=GFN1-xTB, 1=GFN2-xTB, 2=GFN-FF */, int level /* 0..7, crude..extreme */, int threadsSetting /* 0 = auto */)`; `void stop()` (sets atomic stop flag); `void setDraggedAtom(int index)` (−1 = none); `void notifyDragPosition(int index, const std::vector<double>& positionBohr)`; signals: `void progress(int evaluation, int maxEvaluations, double energyHartree)`, `void coordsReady(const std::vector<double>& coordsBohr)`, `void converged(double finalEnergyHartree)`, `void setupFailed(const QString& reason)`. `setup()` must: (a) return false and NOT start the thread if `!XtbApi::isAvailable()`; (b) call the thread/environment bootstrap of task 3.6 first; (c) create the four xTB objects via function pointers under the engine mutex; (d) call the right `loadGFNxx` for the method, then `checkEnvironment` — on failure emit `setupFailed` exactly once with the `xtb_getError` text, clean up all four objects, return false (one attempt only — spec); (e) return true on success. Unit conversions: Å→bohr `1.8897259886`, bohr→Å `0.52917721092` as file-local constexpr. Add `xtbengine.cpp` to the library sources list next to task 1.3's registration. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target avogadro -j8` succeeds.

[OpenSpec 9] 3.2 New test binary `libavogadro/tests/xtbenginetest.cpp` + target `xtbengine` in the plain `tests` list (no xTB linkage). Add the first slots: `setupUnavailableIsHarmless` (if `!XtbApi::isAvailable()`, assert `setup(...)` returns false and `setupFailed` is NOT emitted — use `QSignalSpy`; else QSKIP), `waterSetupSucceeds` (QSKIP when unavailable; setup water {8,1,1} GFN2 level normal → true), `unsupportedElementFailsSetupOnce` (QSKIP when unavailable; setup {8, 99, 1} GFN2 → `setupFailed` received exactly once, `setup()` returns false; calling `setup()` again after cleanup also fails exactly once — no retries leak state). — Verify: `cmake --build build --target xtbengine -j8 && xvfb-run ctest -R xtbengine --output-on-failure` green.

[OpenSpec 10] 3.3 Singlepoint + snapshot plumbing. In `XtbEngine`, implement `run()` as a loop that: copies the current coordinate vector (worker-owned, seeded from setup), performs ONE evaluate step per loop iteration (update molecule coords via `xtb_updateMolecule`, `xtb_singlepoint`, `xtb_getEnergy`, `xtb_getGradient` — all under the engine mutex, worker-only), emits `progress(...)` and `coordsReady(...)` with the current coordinates, then waits on a QWaitCondition (or short sleep, max 50 ms) until the next tick is permitted — the engine does NOT self-loop as fast as possible; the TOOL drives tick pacing by calling the public `void requestTick()` (add it) so GUI apply-rate controls CPU (this mirrors AutoOpt's timer-driven `update()`; the timer lives in the tool, task 4.3). Assert in `run()` that no call is made after `stop()` was observed. Test slots to add in `xtbenginetest.cpp`: `singlepointWaterEnergyNegative` (setup water, `requestTick()`, wait ≤ 5 s in a `QTRY_` loop for `progress` with evaluation ≥ 1, assert the energy argument < 0.0), `coordsReadyRoundTrips` (same setup, assert `coordsReady` delivers 9 doubles for water). — Verify: build + `xvfb-run ctest -R xtbengine --output-on-failure` green.

[OpenSpec 11] 3.4 L-BFGS integration, levels, convergence, cap. In `XtbEngine::run()`, replace the naive per-tick single gradient step with: on each `requestTick()`, run ONE L-BFGS iteration state machine — keep an `LBfgs` member; the evaluate callback does exactly one `updateMolecule+singlepoint+getEnergy+getGradient` (this is the evaluation the callback counts), checks the drag mask of task 3.5 (zero the dragged atom's 3 gradient entries and pin its 3 coordinates before returning), and the loop continues across ticks until: `gradNorm < kXtbLevelThresholds[level]` → emit `converged(finalEnergy)` and stop evaluating; `evaluations >= kXtbMaxEvaluations` (new file-local constant = 500) → emit `converged(lastEnergy)` too (spec: capped sessions stop, cap ≠ error); `shouldStop` (engine stop flag) → exit cleanly. Define the threshold table as a file-local constexpr array of 8 doubles in Eh/bohr, in design D5's order crude…extreme: `{5e-3, 1e-3, 8e-4, 5e-4, 3e-4, 1e-4, 3e-5, 1e-6}` with a comment "approximate xtb optimizer level thresholds — tunable". Reset `LBfgs::resetHistory()` whenever the dragged atom index changes (task 3.5 wires that). Test slots: `waterConvergesToReferenceGeometry` (QSKIP when unavailable; water O at origin, H1 at (0,0,1.3 Å), H2 at (0, 0.1 Å, −0.95 Å), GFN2, level normal (index 4); pump `requestTick()` from a 30 ms QTimer in the test until `converged` OR 60 s timeout; assert O–H lengths in (0.86, 1.06) Å and angle in (94.5°, 114.5°), computing lengths from the last `coordsReady` payload converted to Å), `convergedStopsEvaluations` (after `converged`, record the `progress` evaluation counter, pump 20 more ticks, assert the counter did not increase). — Verify: build + `xvfb-run ctest -R xtbengine --output-on-failure` green (water convergence may take tens of seconds; that is acceptable for this test).

[OpenSpec 12] 3.5 Drag masking + pointer authority. Extend `XtbEngine`: member `m_draggedIndex` (−1 none) settable from any thread via mutex; `notifyDragPosition` stores the pointer-authored position for that atom (bohr). In the evaluate callback (task 3.4) when `m_draggedIndex >= 0`: overwrite that atom's 3 coordinates in the working array with the notified position BEFORE `updateMolecule`, and zero its 3 gradient entries AFTER `getGradient`; the atom's published coordinates therefore always equal the pointer position (spec coordinate write-back). On every change of `m_draggedIndex` (including −1→index and index→−1) call `LBfgs::resetHistory()`. Test slots: `draggedAtomPinnedDuringOptimization` (QSKIP when unavailable; setup water GFN2; start ticking; after ≥ 1 evaluation call `setDraggedAtom(1)` + `notifyDragPosition(1, {0.0, 0.0, 2.0/0.52917721092})` (≈2 Å along z in bohr) and keep ticking with fresh `notifyDragPosition` each tick; after ≥ 3 more evaluations read the last `coordsReady`, convert to Å, assert |H1 − (0,0,2.0)| < 1e-6 Å and that atom 0 and 2 coordinates CHANGED since the drag began — proving the rest relaxed while the dragged atom was pinned), `dragReleaseResumesCoverage` (continue the same flow: `setDraggedAtom(-1)`, pump ticks ≥ 3 evaluations, assert H1's coordinate is no longer exactly the pinned position). — Verify: build + `xvfb-run ctest -R xtbengine --output-on-failure` green.

[OpenSpec 13] 3.6 Interactive accuracy adaptation + threads env. Extend `XtbEngine::setup()` to FIRST apply the OpenMP environment via `qputenv` when the variable is unset: `OMP_WAIT_POLICY=PASSIVE` always; `OMP_NUM_THREADS` = `threadsSetting` if > 0 else auto (`qMax(1, qMin(8, QThread::idealThreadCount() - 1))`) — read-back with `qEnvironmentVariableIsSet` so a user's own env wins (design D7). Add public `void setInteractive(bool interactive)`; when interactive becomes true call `xtb_setAccuracy(env, calc, 0.2)` + `xtb_setMaxIter(env, calc, 30)` under the mutex; when false restore `1.0` / `100` — file-local constexpr `kXtbInteractiveAccuracy=0.2`, `kXtbInteractiveMaxIter=30`, `kXtbDefaultAccuracy=1.0`, `kXtbDefaultMaxIter=100` with a "tunable" comment. Reset L-BFGS history on each toggle (D6). ALSO call `setInteractive(true)`/`setInteractive(false)` automatically from the drag transitions of task 3.5. Test slots: `interactiveTogglesAccuracy` (QSKIP when unavailable; setup water; expose the applied accuracy by adding a getter `double currentAccuracy() const` on the engine; toggle and assert 0.2 then 1.0), `threadsEnvAutoRespectsClamp` (unset `OMP_NUM_THREADS` via `qunsetenv`, call `setup()` with 0, assert `qgetenv("OMP_NUM_THREADS").toInt()` is in [1,8]; then call setup with 3 and assert it equals 3; finally `qunsetenv("OMP_NUM_THREADS")` to not pollute other tests). — Verify: build + `xvfb-run ctest -R xtbengine --output-on-failure` green.

[OpenSpec 14] 3.7 GFN-FF parameter data locator (design D8). Create `libavogadro/src/xtb/xtbparams.h` + `libavogadro/src/xtb/xtbparams.cpp`, namespace `Avogadro::XtbParams`, one function: `bool ensureGfnffParameters(QString* diagnostic)` — logic: (1) if `XTBHOME` or `XTBPATH` is already set in the environment, return true untouched (respect user); (2) probe `QCoreApplication::applicationDirPath() + "/share/xtb"`; (3) probe `"/usr/share/xtb"`; a probe succeeds only if directory exists AND contains `.param_gfnff.xtb`; (4) on success `qputenv("XTBHOME", <dir>)` and `qputenv("XTBPATH", <dir>)` and return true; (5) on failure set a diagnostic naming the probed paths and return false. `XtbEngine::setup()` must call this BEFORE `xtb_loadGFNFF` when `method == 2`, and on false emit `setupFailed(diagnostic)` (once, clean up, return false — the spec's GFN-FF-without-data scenario). GFN1/GFN2 setups must NOT call the locator (no data files needed). Register the two files in the library sources like task 1.3. Test slots in `xtbenginetest.cpp`: `gfnffWaterSetupWhenParamsAvailable` (call `ensureGfnffParameters`; if false → `QSKIP("GFN-FF parameter data not available on this machine")`; else setup water method 2 → true), `gfnffWithoutParamsFailsDeterministically` (only runs when `ensureGfnffParameters` returns false — assert `setup()` returns false and `setupFailed` fired exactly once with a message mentioning "XTBHOME" or "param"; otherwise QSKIP). — Verify: build + `xvfb-run ctest -R xtbengine --output-on-failure` green (on this runner `/usr/share/xtb` is absent unless the `xtb` package is installed — both paths must pass).

[OpenSpec 15] 3.8 Quiesce safety. Extend `XtbEngine` teardown to the AutoOpt pattern: `stop()` sets the flag and wakes the wait condition; destructor runs `stop()`, then `wait()` (guarding `isRunning()`); the four xTB objects are deleted ONLY on the worker thread after its loop observed the stop flag and the current singlepoint returned — implement by having `run()` own deletion at exit and `setup()` only create; add a `bool m_quiesced` guard so `run()` deletes exactly once. Add a mutex rule comment: the GUI thread NEVER calls `xtb_del*` — it only calls `stop()` and `wait()`. Test slot: `immediateStopIsSafe` (QSKIP when unavailable; setup water, `start()`, call `stop()` within 1 ms (do not requestTick), `wait()` with a 10 s timeout asserting it returns true; then setup water again successfully — proving objects were rebuilt cleanly; repeat the whole cycle 5 times in one slot). — Verify: build + `xvfb-run ctest -R xtbengine --output-on-failure` green, then the full suite: `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` shows no new failures (this validates no state leaked into other tests).

[OpenSpec 16] 4.1 Engine selector UI + persistence. In `libavogadro/src/tools/autoopttool.cpp` `settingsWidget()`: add `QComboBox* m_comboEngine` (member in `autoopttool.h`) ABOVE the existing force-field combo, with entries in this order: "Force field", "xTB — GFN1-xTB", "xTB — GFN2-xTB", "xTB — GFN-FF" (constants `enum Engine { ForceField=0, Gfn1=1, Gfn2=2, GfnFf=3 };` in the header). When engine != ForceField: hide `m_comboFF` and `m_comboAlgorithm` (the FF-only controls) and show the xTB controls (add `QComboBox* m_comboLevel` with the 8 level names "Crude…Extreme", default index 4 = Normal, and reuse/keep the existing `m_stepsSpinBox`); when ForceField: the reverse. Persist via the tool's existing `writeSettings`/`readSettings` under keys `engine` and `xtbLevel`. Connect `currentIndexChanged` to a `void engineChanged()` slot doing the show/hide. MSVC-safe plain widgets only. Do NOT touch FF behavior yet. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target autoopttool -j8` succeeds and `xvfb-run ctest -R autooptrepro --output-on-failure` stays green.

[OpenSpec 17] 4.2 Availability gating. In `engineChanged()` and in `enable()`: when engine is an xTB entry and `!XtbApi::isAvailable()`, disable the Start button (`m_buttonStartStop->setEnabled(false)`), set its tooltip to "xTB library not found — force fields remain available", and emit the tool `message` signal with the same text (visible diagnostic — spec). When ForceField (or xTB with library present), restore enabled state. Do not change FF availability logic. — Verify: build target `autoopttool`; add a slot `xtbEngineGatedWithoutLibrary` to `libavogadro/tests/autooptreprotest.cpp` (follow that file's existing fixture pattern): construct the tool, read the settings widget, set engine combo to GFN2; if `!XtbApi::isAvailable()` assert the Start button `!isEnabled()`, else assert `isEnabled()`; `xvfb-run ctest -R autooptrepro --output-on-failure` green.

[OpenSpec 18] 4.3 Session routing. In `AutoOptTool::enable()`: branch on engine. ForceField path: exactly the existing code, unchanged. xTB path: collect `atomicNumbers` + `positionsAngstrom` from the molecule, call `m_xtbEngine->setup(numbers, positions, engineToMethod(engine), m_comboLevel->currentIndex(), m_threadsSpinBox ? m_threadsSpinBox->value() : 0)` (add member `XtbEngine* m_xtbEngine = nullptr;` created in the constructor, deleted in the destructor with `stop(); wait();` semantics per task 3.8 — the engine destructor handles it; do NOT delete while running). On setup failure show the failed-setup diagnostic in the HUD path (set a `m_setupFailed`-style flag already used by the FF path) and do not start. On success: `m_xtbEngine->start(QThread::LowPriority)`, start a `QBasicTimer` tick at 100 ms whose `timerEvent` calls `m_xtbEngine->requestTick()` and, if a `coordsReady` snapshot is pending (engine adds `bool takeLatestCoords(std::vector<double>& out)` returning false when nothing new, guarded by mutex), applies the snapshot to the molecule: molecule write lock (follow exactly how the FF path applies coordinates — same lock object and pattern), convert bohr→Å per atom index, `Atom::setPos`, then `Molecule::update()` + `GLWidget::update()`. Disable(): for xTB do `m_xtbEngine->stop()` then `quit()` is NOT needed (engine is not an event loop) — call `wait()` guarded by `isRunning()`, matching the engine's quiesce contract (3.8). The existing `abort()` connections (molecule destroyed, tool deactivated) must ALSO stop the xTB engine — extend them to a shared `void stopEngine()` private helper that quiesces whichever engine is active. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target autoopttool -j8` and `xvfb-run ctest -R autooptrepro --output-on-failure` green.

[OpenSpec 19] 4.4 Drag routing. In `AutoOptTool::mousePressEvent` / `mouseMoveEvent` / `mouseReleaseEvent`: the FF path is untouched. For xTB sessions: on press compute the clicked atom index exactly as the FF path does; on move, translate the clicked atom's position via the existing `translate()` helper (pointer authority — this already writes the molecule position under the GUI's rules), then forward to the engine: `m_xtbEngine->setDraggedAtom(idx)` on press, `notifyDragPosition(idx, <pos in bohr>)` on every move, `setDraggedAtom(-1)` on release; the engine's masking (task 3.5) guarantees write-back never regresses the dragged atom (spec). Convert Å→bohr at this boundary (1.8897259886). Do not add fix markers on the xTB path (they are FF-only). — Verify: build + `xvfb-run ctest -R autooptrepro --output-on-failure` green; add slot `xtbDragCycleLeavesValidMolecule` to `autooptreprotest.cpp` (QSKIP when `!XtbApi::isAvailable()`; construct tool + molecule water GFN2 engine, simulate enable via the tool's public API paths used by other slots in that file, synthesize press/move/release on the widget fixture as the file already does for FF, then disable; assert molecule atom count intact and positions finite).

[OpenSpec 20] 4.5 HUD per engine. In `AutoOptTool::paint()`: keep the FF HUD exactly; for an active xTB session draw, at the same position style, `tr("xTB %1: E = %2 kJ/mol")` where %1 is the method name ("GFN1-xTB"/"GFN2-xTB"/"GFN-FF") and %2 is `energyHartree * 2625.499748` fed from the `progress` signal (connect `progress` to a slot storing the last energy, as the FF path stores its energy); also show the converged state by drawing the final energy once after `converged` fires (the session stays open, evaluations stopped — spec). Setup failures draw the existing failure text pattern with the engine's reason string. — Verify: build + `xvfb-run ctest -R "autooptrepro|energyhud" --output-on-failure` green.

[OpenSpec 21] 4.6 Settings smoke. Add slot `engineSettingsRoundTrip` to `libavogadro/tests/autooptreprotest.cpp`: construct the tool, `settingsWidget()`, set engine GFN2 + level Tight, `writeSettings` into a temp `QSettings` (temp ini file, delete after), construct a second tool instance, `readSettings`, assert engine == GFN2 and level == Tight. — Verify: `xvfb-run ctest -R autooptrepro --output-on-failure` green.

Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-xtb-optimization" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-xtb-optimization" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Done when:

1. "openspec instructions apply --change add-xtb-optimization --json" reports zero remaining required implementation tasks.

2. Every explicit requirement and scenario in the active OpenSpec change has corresponding implementation evidence.

3. OpenSpec task completion accurately reflects the actual codebase state; no checkbox is marked complete merely because work was attempted.

4. Relevant builds, tests, and regression checks pass.

6. A final comparison of the OpenSpec artifacts against the resulting implementation finds no substantive omission.

7. The repository is left in a coherent state suitable for subsequent OpenSpec verification/archive work.

8. Every mirrored GLLA task is complete (the GLLA task list shows no open tasks), so GLLA's pending-task gate does not refuse completion.

Do not declare the GLLA goal complete based only on previous conversation claims or task checkboxes. Verify against current repository and OpenSpec evidence.

[OpenSpec 6] 2.1 Create `libavogadro/src/xtb/lbfgs.h` + `libavogadro/src/xtb/lbfgs.cpp`, namespace `Avogadro::Xtb`, class `LBfgs`. Public surface (fixed by design D5 — implement exactly this): constructor takes nothing; `void setHistory(int m)` (default constant `kLBfgsHistory = 10`); `struct Result { bool converged; int evaluations; double finalGradNorm; };`; `template <typename Eval, typename Stop> Result minimize(std::vector<double>& coords, Eval&& evaluate, Stop&& shouldStop)` — `evaluate` has signature `double(const std::vector<double>& coords, std::vector<double>& grad)` returning energy and filling the gradient of equal length; `shouldStop` has signature `bool(int evaluations)` returning true when the caller wants to stop (cancelled/max cap). Also `void resetHistory()`. Implementation: standard two-loop recursion L-BFGS with a backtracking Armijo line search (initial step 1.0, shrink factor 0.5, `c1 = 1e-4`, at most 20 shrink steps per iteration; fall back to a small fixed step `1e-3` scaled by inverse gradient norm if Armijo never accepts — never loop forever); convergence is caller-declared: add `double gradNorm(const std::vector<double>&) const` helper and let the CALLER compare against thresholds (the engine owns thresholds per D5). Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-xtb-optimization" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-xtb-optimization" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Done when:

1. "openspec instructions apply --change add-xtb-optimization --json" reports zero remaining required implementation tasks.

2. Every explicit requirement and scenario in the active OpenSpec change has corresponding implementation evidence.

3. OpenSpec task completion accurately reflects the actual codebase state; no checkbox is marked complete merely because work was attempted.

4. Relevant builds, tests, and regression checks pass.

5. No known required work, implementation blocker, knowingly failing relevant test, or silently deferred required task remains.

6. A final comparison of the OpenSpec artifacts against the resulting implementation finds no substantive omission.

7. The repository is left in a coherent state suitable for subsequent OpenSpec verification/archive work.

8. Every mirrored GLLA task is complete (the GLLA task list shows no open tasks), so GLLA's pending-task gate does not refuse completion.

Do not declare the GLLA goal complete based only on previous conversation claims or task checkboxes. Verify against current repository and OpenSpec evidence.

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1] 1.1 Vendor the xTB API header. Create directory `libavogadro/src/xtb/`. Copy the xTB C API header into `libavogadro/src/xtb/xtb.h` — take it verbatim from the Ubuntu package `libxtb-dev` 6.6.1 (`/usr/include/xtb.h`; if not installed: `cd /tmp && apt-get download libxtb-dev && dpkg -x libxtb-dev*.deb ext/ && cp ext/usr/include/xtb.h libavogadro/src/xtb/xtb.h`). Also create `libavogadro/src/xtb/README.md` with three lines: source package+version, upstream project (grimme-lab/xtb), and "header only — the library itself is resolved at runtime, never linked". Do not modify anything else in the header. — Verify: `echo '#include "xtb.h"' > /tmp/hdrcheck.cpp` compiles with `-I libavogadro/src/xtb -fsyntax-only` using g++: `g++ -std=c++17 -I libavogadro/src/xtb -fsyntax-only /tmp/hdrcheck.cpp` exits 0.

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Create the runtime loader `libavogadro/src/xtb/xtbapi.h` + `libavogadro/src/xtb/xtbapi.cpp`, class `Avogadro::XtbApi` (all-static public API, no instances): `static bool isAvailable();` (loads once, caches), `static QString lastError();`, and one static accessor per C function, returning a function pointer or `nullptr` when unavailable. Include `"xtb.h"` from the same directory and declare typedefs for every function pointer used: `xtb_newEnvironment`, `xtb_delEnvironment`, `xtb_checkEnvironment`, `xtb_getError`, `xtb_setVerbosity`, `xtb_newMolecule`, `xtb_delMolecule`, `xtb_updateMolecule`, `xtb_newCalculator`, `xtb_delCalculator`, `xtb_loadGFN0xTB`, `xtb_loadGFN1xTB`, `xtb_loadGFN2xTB`, `xtb_loadGFNFF`, `xtb_setAccuracy`, `xtb_setMaxIter`, `xtb_setElectronicTemp`, `xtb_singlepoint`, `xtb_newResults`, `xtb_delResults`, `xtb_getEnergy`, `xtb_getGradient`. Loading: `QLibrary` tried in order `libxtb-6` (Windows), `libxtb.so.6`, `libxtb.so` (non-Windows); resolve via `QLibrary::resolve`; on total failure set the error string naming the tried names and return false from `isAvailable()`. Thread-safety: guard the one-time load with a `QMutex` (static). No MOC needed (no `Q_OBJECT`). — Verify: `cmake --build build --target avogadro -j8` succeeds after 1.3 registers the files.

[OpenSpec 3] 1.3 Register the shim in the library build. In `libavogadro/src/CMakeLists.txt` add `xtb/xtbapi.cpp` to `libavogadro_SRCS` (or the equivalent sources list used there) and `xtb/xtbapi.h` + `xtb/xtb.h` to the headers list, following how existing subdirectory sources are added in that file. Do not add any find/link of xTB. — Verify: `cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build --target avogadro -j8` succeeds, and `nm -D build/libavogadro/libavogadro.so* 2>/dev/null | grep -c XtbApi` is > 0 (symbols exported), and the configure log contains NO new xTB-related find output.

[OpenSpec 4] 1.4 New test `libavogadro/tests/xtbruntimetest.cpp` + target. Test class `XtbRuntimeTest`, two slots: `absentIsHarmless` — if `XtbApi::isAvailable()` is false, assert `lastError()` is non-empty and return (QSKIP is also acceptable); if true, QSKIP with "library present" (this slot only checks the absent path); `waterGfn2Singlepoint` — QSKIP when `!XtbApi::isAvailable()`; otherwise build a water molecule through the function pointers (O + 2 H exactly as in the existing `libavogadro/tests/xtbphysicstest.cpp` coordinates), run `loadGFN2xTB` + `singlepoint` + `getEnergy`, `QVERIFY(energy < 0.0)`, and free all four objects in order (results, calculator, molecule, environment). Add `xtbruntime` to the `tests` list in `libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt` (the plain list near the top, NOT inside any `if(XTB_FOUND)` block) — the target builds with no xTB linkage. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target xtbruntimetest -j8 && xvfb-run ctest -R xtbruntimetest --output-on-failure` passes (on this machine the library may be absent → skips; on the CI `xtb=ON` leg it runs).

[OpenSpec 5] 1.5 Rewrite `libavogadro/tests/xtbphysicstest.cpp` onto the shim. Replace `#include <xtb.h>` with `#include "xtb/xtbapi.h"` (adjust include path per how tests include library headers — follow the pattern of the includes already at the top of `xtbphysicstest.cpp`), route every xTB call through the `XtbApi` function pointers, add `if (!XtbApi::isAvailable()) QSKIP("xTB runtime library not available");` as the first line of `energy()`, and delete the energy/gradient call differences only as needed — the test keeps its single `energy()` slot asserting `energy < 0.0` for water GFN2. In `libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt` remove `xtbphysics` from the `if(XTB_FOUND) list(APPEND tests ...)` line (leave `xtbopttool` there — it is removed later in task 6.1) and add `xtbphysics` to the plain `tests` list; delete the now-dead lines `target_link_libraries(xtbphysicstest PRIVATE ${XTB_LIBRARIES})` and the matching OpenMP line for `xtbphysicstest` only (keep `xtbopttooltest`'s lines — still needed until task 6.1). — Verify: `cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build --target xtbphysicstest -j8 && xvfb-run ctest -R xtbphysicstest --output-on-failure` passes, and `grep -c "XTB_LIBRARIES" libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt` shows only `xtbopttooltest` occurrences remain.

[OpenSpec 6] 2.1 Create `libavogadro/src/xtb/lbfgs.h` + `libavogadro/src/xtb/lbfgs.cpp`, namespace `Avogadro::Xtb`, class `LBfgs`. Public surface (fixed by design D5 — implement exactly this): constructor takes nothing; `void setHistory(int m)` (default constant `kLBfgsHistory = 10`); `struct Result { bool converged; int evaluations; double finalGradNorm; };`; `template <typename Eval, typename Stop> Result minimize(std::vector<double>& coords, Eval&& evaluate, Stop&& shouldStop)` — `evaluate` has signature `double(const std::vector<double>& coords, std::vector<double>& grad)` returning energy and filling the gradient of equal length; `shouldStop` has signature `bool(int evaluations)` returning true when the caller wants to stop (cancelled/max cap). Also `void resetHistory()`. Implementation: standard two-loop recursion L-BFGS with a backtracking Armijo line search (initial step 1.0, shrink factor 0.5, `c1 = 1e-4`, at most 20 shrink steps per iteration; fall back to a small fixed step `1e-3` scaled by inverse gradient norm if Armijo never accepts — never loop forever); convergence is caller-declared: add `double gradNorm(const std::vector<double>&) const` helper and let the CALLER compare against thresholds (the engine owns thresholds per D5). All plain `std::vector`/`<cmath>` — no Qt, no Eigen, no xTB includes. MSVC-safe. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target avogadro -j8` after 2.3 registers the file.

[OpenSpec 7] 2.2 New test `libavogadro/tests/lbfgstest.cpp` + target `lbfgstest` (add `lbfgs` to the plain `tests` list in `libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt` — no library linkage beyond the avogadro lib). Four slots: `quadraticConverges` (2-atom flat system: f = sum((x-3)^2), grad = 2(x-3), assert final grad norm < 1e-6 within 100 evaluations), `rosenbrockConverges` (2-variable Rosenbrock a=1 b=100 from (-1.2, 1.0), assert |x-1| < 1e-2 within 1000 evaluations), `maxEvaluationsStops` (same Rosenbrock but `shouldStop` returns true at 10 evaluations; assert `Result::evaluations <= 11` and no crash), `historyResetWorks` (run to partial convergence, call `resetHistory()`, run again, assert convergence still reached). — Verify: `cmake --build build --target lbfgstest -j8 && xvfb-run ctest -R lbfgstest --output-on-failure` green.

[OpenSpec 8] 3.1 Engine skeleton + setup lifecycle. Create `libavogadro/src/xtb/xtbengine.h` + `libavogadro/src/xtb/xtbengine.cpp`, class `Avogadro::XtbEngine : public QThread` (follow the structure of `AutoOptThread` in `libavogadro/src/tools/autoopttool.h` — constructor/destructor, `setup(...)`, `run()`, `stop()`, signals). Public surface (fixed — implement exactly this): `bool setup(const std::vector<int>& atomicNumbers, const std::vector<double>& positionsAngstrom, int method /* 0=GFN1-xTB, 1=GFN2-xTB, 2=GFN-FF */, int level /* 0..7, crude..extreme */, int threadsSetting /* 0 = auto */)`; `void stop()` (sets atomic stop flag); `void setDraggedAtom(int index)` (−1 = none); `void notifyDragPosition(int index, const std::vector<double>& positionBohr)`; signals: `void progress(int evaluation, int maxEvaluations, double energyHartree)`, `void coordsReady(const std::vector<double>& coordsBohr)`, `void converged(double finalEnergyHartree)`, `void setupFailed(const QString& reason)`. `setup()` must: (a) return false and NOT start the thread if `!XtbApi::isAvailable()`; (b) call the thread/environment bootstrap of task 3.6 first; (c) create the four xTB objects via function pointers under the engine mutex; (d) call the right `loadGFNxx` for the method, then `checkEnvironment` — on failure emit `setupFailed` exactly once with the `xtb_getError` text, clean up all four objects, return false (one attempt only — spec); (e) return true on success. Unit conversions: Å→bohr `1.8897259886`, bohr→Å `0.52917721092` as file-local constexpr. Add `xtbengine.cpp` to the library sources list next to task 1.3's registration. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target avogadro -j8` succeeds.

[OpenSpec 9] 3.2 New test binary `libavogadro/tests/xtbenginetest.cpp` + target `xtbengine` in the plain `tests` list (no xTB linkage). Add the first slots: `setupUnavailableIsHarmless` (if `!XtbApi::isAvailable()`, assert `setup(...)` returns false and `setupFailed` is NOT emitted — use `QSignalSpy`; else QSKIP), `waterSetupSucceeds` (QSKIP when unavailable; setup water {8,1,1} GFN2 level normal → true), `unsupportedElementFailsSetupOnce` (QSKIP when unavailable; setup {8, 99, 1} GFN2 → `setupFailed` received exactly once, `setup()` returns false; calling `setup()` again after cleanup also fails exactly once — no retries leak state). — Verify: `cmake --build build --target xtbengine -j8 && xvfb-run ctest -R xtbengine --output-on-failure` green.

[OpenSpec 10] 3.3 Singlepoint + snapshot plumbing. In `XtbEngine`, implement `run()` as a loop that: copies the current coordinate vector (worker-owned, seeded from setup), performs ONE evaluate step per loop iteration (update molecule coords via `xtb_updateMolecule`, `xtb_singlepoint`, `xtb_getEnergy`, `xtb_getGradient` — all under the engine mutex, worker-only), emits `progress(...)` and `coordsReady(...)` with the current coordinates, then waits on a QWaitCondition (or short sleep, max 50 ms) until the next tick is permitted — the engine does NOT self-loop as fast as possible; the TOOL drives tick pacing by calling the public `void requestTick()` (add it) so GUI apply-rate controls CPU (this mirrors AutoOpt's timer-driven `update()`; the timer lives in the tool, task 4.3). Assert in `run()` that no call is made after `stop()` was observed. Test slots to add in `xtbenginetest.cpp`: `singlepointWaterEnergyNegative` (setup water, `requestTick()`, wait ≤ 5 s in a `QTRY_` loop for `progress` with evaluation ≥ 1, assert the energy argument < 0.0), `coordsReadyRoundTrips` (same setup, assert `coordsReady` delivers 9 doubles for water). — Verify: build + `xvfb-run ctest -R xtbengine --output-on-failure` green.

[OpenSpec 11] 3.4 L-BFGS integration, levels, convergence, cap. In `XtbEngine::run()`, replace the naive per-tick single gradient step with: on each `requestTick()`, run ONE L-BFGS iteration state machine — keep an `LBfgs` member; the evaluate callback does exactly one `updateMolecule+singlepoint+getEnergy+getGradient` (this is the evaluation the callback counts), checks the drag mask of task 3.5 (zero the dragged atom's 3 gradient entries and pin its 3 coordinates before returning), and the loop continues across ticks until: `gradNorm < kXtbLevelThresholds[level]` → emit `converged(finalEnergy)` and stop evaluating; `evaluations >= kXtbMaxEvaluations` (new file-local constant = 500) → emit `converged(lastEnergy)` too (spec: capped sessions stop, cap ≠ error); `shouldStop` (engine stop flag) → exit cleanly. Define the threshold table as a file-local constexpr array of 8 doubles in Eh/bohr, in design D5's order crude…extreme: `{5e-3, 1e-3, 8e-4, 5e-4, 3e-4, 1e-4, 3e-5, 1e-6}` with a comment "approximate xtb optimizer level thresholds — tunable". Reset `LBfgs::resetHistory()` whenever the dragged atom index changes (task 3.5 wires that). Test slots: `waterConvergesToReferenceGeometry` (QSKIP when unavailable; water O at origin, H1 at (0,0,1.3 Å), H2 at (0, 0.1 Å, −0.95 Å), GFN2, level normal (index 4); pump `requestTick()` from a 30 ms QTimer in the test until `converged` OR 60 s timeout; assert O–H lengths in (0.86, 1.06) Å and angle in (94.5°, 114.5°), computing lengths from the last `coordsReady` payload converted to Å), `convergedStopsEvaluations` (after `converged`, record the `progress` evaluation counter, pump 20 more ticks, assert the counter did not increase). — Verify: build + `xvfb-run ctest -R xtbengine --output-on-failure` green (water convergence may take tens of seconds; that is acceptable for this test).

[OpenSpec 12] 3.5 Drag masking + pointer authority. Extend `XtbEngine`: member `m_draggedIndex` (−1 none) settable from any thread via mutex; `notifyDragPosition` stores the pointer-authored position for that atom (bohr). In the evaluate callback (task 3.4) when `m_draggedIndex >= 0`: overwrite that atom's 3 coordinates in the working array with the notified position BEFORE `updateMolecule`, and zero its 3 gradient entries AFTER `getGradient`; the atom's published coordinates therefore always equal the pointer position (spec coordinate write-back). On every change of `m_draggedIndex` (including −1→index and index→−1) call `LBfgs::resetHistory()`. Test slots: `draggedAtomPinnedDuringOptimization` (QSKIP when unavailable; setup water GFN2; start ticking; after ≥ 1 evaluation call `setDraggedAtom(1)` + `notifyDragPosition(1, {0.0, 0.0, 2.0/0.52917721092})` (≈2 Å along z in bohr) and keep ticking with fresh `notifyDragPosition` each tick; after ≥ 3 more evaluations read the last `coordsReady`, convert to Å, assert |H1 − (0,0,2.0)| < 1e-6 Å and that atom 0 and 2 coordinates CHANGED since the drag began — proving the rest relaxed while the dragged atom was pinned), `dragReleaseResumesCoverage` (continue the same flow: `setDraggedAtom(-1)`, pump ticks ≥ 3 evaluations, assert H1's coordinate is no longer exactly the pinned position). — Verify: build + `xvfb-run ctest -R xtbengine --output-on-failure` green.

Update `AutoOptTool`'s `AVOGADRO_TOOL` tooltip/description in `autoopttool.h` to name all four engines (force fields, GFN1-xTB, GFN2-xTB, GFN-FF), that atoms can be pulled during optimization, and the convergence-level control. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target autoopttool -j8` and a slot in `autooptreprotest.cpp` asserting `tool->toolTip()`/description text (whichever accessor the Tool API exposes) contains "GFN2-xTB"; `xvfb-run ctest -R autooptrepro --output-on-failure` green.

Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-xtb-optimization" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-xtb-optimization" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Done when:

1. "openspec instructions apply --change add-xtb-optimization --json" reports zero remaining required implementation tasks.

2. Every explicit requirement and scenario in the active OpenSpec change has corresponding implementation evidence.

3. OpenSpec task completion accurately reflects the actual codebase state; no checkbox is marked complete merely because work was attempted.

4. Relevant builds, tests, and regression checks pass.

5. No known required work, implementation blocker, knowingly failing relevant test, or silently deferred required task remains.

6. A final comparison of the OpenSpec artifacts against the resulting implementation finds no substantive omission.

7. The repository is left in a coherent state suitable for subsequent OpenSpec verification/archive work.

8. Every mirrored GLLA task is complete (the GLLA task list shows no open tasks), so GLLA's pending-task gate does not refuse completion.

Do not declare the GLLA goal complete based only on previous conversation claims or task checkboxes. Verify against current repository and OpenSpec evidence.

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1] 1.1 Vendor the xTB API header. Create directory `libavogadro/src/xtb/`. Copy the xTB C API header into `libavogadro/src/xtb/xtb.h` — take it verbatim from the Ubuntu package `libxtb-dev` 6.6.1 (`/usr/include/xtb.h`; if not installed: `cd /tmp && apt-get download libxtb-dev && dpkg -x libxtb-dev*.deb ext/ && cp ext/usr/include/xtb.h libavogadro/src/xtb/xtb.h`). Also create `libavogadro/src/xtb/README.md` with three lines: source package+version, upstream project (grimme-lab/xtb), and "header only — the library itself is resolved at runtime, never linked". Do not modify anything else in the header. — Verify: `echo '#include "xtb.h"' > /tmp/hdrcheck.cpp` compiles with `-I libavogadro/src/xtb -fsyntax-only` using g++: `g++ -std=c++17 -I libavogadro/src/xtb -fsyntax-only /tmp/hdrcheck.cpp` exits 0.

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Create the runtime loader `libavogadro/src/xtb/xtbapi.h` + `libavogadro/src/xtb/xtbapi.cpp`, class `Avogadro::XtbApi` (all-static public API, no instances): `static bool isAvailable();` (loads once, caches), `static QString lastError();`, and one static accessor per C function, returning a function pointer or `nullptr` when unavailable. Include `"xtb.h"` from the same directory and declare typedefs for every function pointer used: `xtb_newEnvironment`, `xtb_delEnvironment`, `xtb_checkEnvironment`, `xtb_getError`, `xtb_setVerbosity`, `xtb_newMolecule`, `xtb_delMolecule`, `xtb_updateMolecule`, `xtb_newCalculator`, `xtb_delCalculator`, `xtb_loadGFN0xTB`, `xtb_loadGFN1xTB`, `xtb_loadGFN2xTB`, `xtb_loadGFNFF`, `xtb_setAccuracy`, `xtb_setMaxIter`, `xtb_setElectronicTemp`, `xtb_singlepoint`, `xtb_newResults`, `xtb_delResults`, `xtb_getEnergy`, `xtb_getGradient`. Loading: `QLibrary` tried in order `libxtb-6` (Windows), `libxtb.so.6`, `libxtb.so` (non-Windows); resolve via `QLibrary::resolve`; on total failure set the error string naming the tried names and return false from `isAvailable()`. Thread-safety: guard the one-time load with a `QMutex` (static). No MOC needed (no `Q_OBJECT`). — Verify: `cmake --build build --target avogadro -j8` succeeds after 1.3 registers the files.

[OpenSpec 3] 1.3 Register the shim in the library build. In `libavogadro/src/CMakeLists.txt` add `xtb/xtbapi.cpp` to `libavogadro_SRCS` (or the equivalent sources list used there) and `xtb/xtbapi.h` + `xtb/xtb.h` to the headers list, following how existing subdirectory sources are added in that file. Do not add any find/link of xTB. — Verify: `cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build --target avogadro -j8` succeeds, and `nm -D build/libavogadro/libavogadro.so* 2>/dev/null | grep -c XtbApi` is > 0 (symbols exported), and the configure log contains NO new xTB-related find output.

[OpenSpec 4] 1.4 New test `libavogadro/tests/xtbruntimetest.cpp` + target. Test class `XtbRuntimeTest`, two slots: `absentIsHarmless` — if `XtbApi::isAvailable()` is false, assert `lastError()` is non-empty and return (QSKIP is also acceptable); if true, QSKIP with "library present" (this slot only checks the absent path); `waterGfn2Singlepoint` — QSKIP when `!XtbApi::isAvailable()`; otherwise build a water molecule through the function pointers (O + 2 H exactly as in the existing `libavogadro/tests/xtbphysicstest.cpp` coordinates), run `loadGFN2xTB` + `singlepoint` + `getEnergy`, `QVERIFY(energy < 0.0)`, and free all four objects in order (results, calculator, molecule, environment). Add `xtbruntime` to the `tests` list in `libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt` (the plain list near the top, NOT inside any `if(XTB_FOUND)` block) — the target builds with no xTB linkage. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target xtbruntimetest -j8 && xvfb-run ctest -R xtbruntimetest --output-on-failure` passes (on this machine the library may be absent → skips; on the CI `xtb=ON` leg it runs).

[OpenSpec 5] 1.5 Rewrite `libavogadro/tests/xtbphysicstest.cpp` onto the shim. Replace `#include <xtb.h>` with `#include "xtb/xtbapi.h"` (adjust include path per how tests include library headers — follow the pattern of the includes already at the top of `xtbphysicstest.cpp`), route every xTB call through the `XtbApi` function pointers, add `if (!XtbApi::isAvailable()) QSKIP("xTB runtime library not available");` as the first line of `energy()`, and delete the energy/gradient call differences only as needed — the test keeps its single `energy()` slot asserting `energy < 0.0` for water GFN2. In `libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt` remove `xtbphysics` from the `if(XTB_FOUND) list(APPEND tests ...)` line (leave `xtbopttool` there — it is removed later in task 6.1) and add `xtbphysics` to the plain `tests` list; delete the now-dead lines `target_link_libraries(xtbphysicstest PRIVATE ${XTB_LIBRARIES})` and the matching OpenMP line for `xtbphysicstest` only (keep `xtbopttooltest`'s lines — still needed until task 6.1). — Verify: `cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build --target xtbphysicstest -j8 && xvfb-run ctest -R xtbphysicstest --output-on-failure` passes, and `grep -c "XTB_LIBRARIES" libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt` shows only `xtbopttooltest` occurrences remain.

[OpenSpec 6] 2.1 Create `libavogadro/src/xtb/lbfgs.h` + `libavogadro/src/xtb/lbfgs.cpp`, namespace `Avogadro::Xtb`, class `LBfgs`. Public surface (fixed by design D5 — implement exactly this): constructor takes nothing; `void setHistory(int m)` (default constant `kLBfgsHistory = 10`); `struct Result { bool converged; int evaluations; double finalGradNorm; };`; `template <typename Eval, typename Stop> Result minimize(std::vector<double>& coords, Eval&& evaluate, Stop&& shouldStop)` — `evaluate` has signature `double(const std::vector<double>& coords, std::vector<double>& grad)` returning energy and filling the gradient of equal length; `shouldStop` has signature `bool(int evaluations)` returning true when the caller wants to stop (cancelled/max cap). Also `void resetHistory()`. Implementation: standard two-loop recursion L-BFGS with a backtracking Armijo line search (initial step 1.0, shrink factor 0.5, `c1 = 1e-4`, at most 20 shrink steps per iteration; fall back to a small fixed step `1e-3` scaled by inverse gradient norm if Armijo never accepts — never loop forever); convergence is caller-declared: add `double gradNorm(const std::vector<double>&) const` helper and let the CALLER compare against thresholds (the engine owns thresholds per D5). All plain `std::vector`/`<cmath>` — no Qt, no Eigen, no xTB includes. MSVC-safe. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target avogadro -j8` after 2.3 registers the file.

[OpenSpec 7] 2.2 New test `libavogadro/tests/lbfgstest.cpp` + target `lbfgstest` (add `lbfgs` to the plain `tests` list in `libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt` — no library linkage beyond the avogadro lib). Four slots: `quadraticConverges` (2-atom flat system: f = sum((x-3)^2), grad = 2(x-3), assert final grad norm < 1e-6 within 100 evaluations), `rosenbrockConverges` (2-variable Rosenbrock a=1 b=100 from (-1.2, 1.0), assert |x-1| < 1e-2 within 1000 evaluations), `maxEvaluationsStops` (same Rosenbrock but `shouldStop` returns true at 10 evaluations; assert `Result::evaluations <= 11` and no crash), `historyResetWorks` (run to partial convergence, call `resetHistory()`, run again, assert convergence still reached). — Verify: `cmake --build build --target lbfgstest -j8 && xvfb-run ctest -R lbfgstest --output-on-failure` green.

[OpenSpec 8] 3.1 Engine skeleton + setup lifecycle. Create `libavogadro/src/xtb/xtbengine.h` + `libavogadro/src/xtb/xtbengine.cpp`, class `Avogadro::XtbEngine : public QThread` (follow the structure of `AutoOptThread` in `libavogadro/src/tools/autoopttool.h` — constructor/destructor, `setup(...)`, `run()`, `stop()`, signals). Public surface (fixed — implement exactly this): `bool setup(const std::vector<int>& atomicNumbers, const std::vector<double>& positionsAngstrom, int method /* 0=GFN1-xTB, 1=GFN2-xTB, 2=GFN-FF */, int level /* 0..7, crude..extreme */, int threadsSetting /* 0 = auto */)`; `void stop()` (sets atomic stop flag); `void setDraggedAtom(int index)` (−1 = none); `void notifyDragPosition(int index, const std::vector<double>& positionBohr)`; signals: `void progress(int evaluation, int maxEvaluations, double energyHartree)`, `void coordsReady(const std::vector<double>& coordsBohr)`, `void converged(double finalEnergyHartree)`, `void setupFailed(const QString& reason)`. `setup()` must: (a) return false and NOT start the thread if `!XtbApi::isAvailable()`; (b) call the thread/environment bootstrap of task 3.6 first; (c) create the four xTB objects via function pointers under the engine mutex; (d) call the right `loadGFNxx` for the method, then `checkEnvironment` — on failure emit `setupFailed` exactly once with the `xtb_getError` text, clean up all four objects, return false (one attempt only — spec); (e) return true on success. Unit conversions: Å→bohr `1.8897259886`, bohr→Å `0.52917721092` as file-local constexpr. Add `xtbengine.cpp` to the library sources list next to task 1.3's registration. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target avogadro -j8` succeeds.

[OpenSpec 9] 3.2 New test binary `libavogadro/tests/xtbenginetest.cpp` + target `xtbengine` in the plain `tests` list (no xTB linkage). Add the first slots: `setupUnavailableIsHarmless` (if `!XtbApi::isAvailable()`, assert `setup(...)` returns false and `setupFailed` is NOT emitted — use `QSignalSpy`; else QSKIP), `waterSetupSucceeds` (QSKIP when unavailable; setup water {8,1,1} GFN2 level normal → true), `unsupportedElementFailsSetupOnce` (QSKIP when unavailable; setup {8, 99, 1} GFN2 → `setupFailed` received exactly once, `setup()` returns false; calling `setup()` again after cleanup also fails exactly once — no retries leak state). — Verify: `cmake --build build --target xtbengine -j8 && xvfb-run ctest -R xtbengine --output-on-failure` green.

[OpenSpec 10] 3.3 Singlepoint + snapshot plumbing. In `XtbEngine`, implement `run()` as a loop that: copies the current coordinate vector (worker-owned, seeded from setup), performs ONE evaluate step per loop iteration (update molecule coords via `xtb_updateMolecule`, `xtb_singlepoint`, `xtb_getEnergy`, `xtb_getGradient` — all under the engine mutex, worker-only), emits `progress(...)` and `coordsReady(...)` with the current coordinates, then waits on a QWaitCondition (or short sleep, max 50 ms) until the next tick is permitted — the engine does NOT self-loop as fast as possible; the TOOL drives tick pacing by calling the public `void requestTick()` (add it) so GUI apply-rate controls CPU (this mirrors AutoOpt's timer-driven `update()`; the timer lives in the tool, task 4.3). Assert in `run()` that no call is made after `stop()` was observed. Test slots to add in `xtbenginetest.cpp`: `singlepointWaterEnergyNegative` (setup water, `requestTick()`, wait ≤ 5 s in a `QTRY_` loop for `progress` with evaluation ≥ 1, assert the energy argument < 0.0), `coordsReadyRoundTrips` (same setup, assert `coordsReady` delivers 9 doubles for water). — Verify: build + `xvfb-run ctest -R xtbengine --output-on-failure` green.

[OpenSpec 11] 3.4 L-BFGS integration, levels, convergence, cap. In `XtbEngine::run()`, replace the naive per-tick single gradient step with: on each `requestTick()`, run ONE L-BFGS iteration state machine — keep an `LBfgs` member; the evaluate callback does exactly one `updateMolecule+singlepoint+getEnergy+getGradient` (this is the evaluation the callback counts), checks the drag mask of task 3.5 (zero the dragged atom's 3 gradient entries and pin its 3 coordinates before returning), and the loop continues across ticks until: `gradNorm < kXtbLevelThresholds[level]` → emit `converged(finalEnergy)` and stop evaluating; `evaluations >= kXtbMaxEvaluations` (new file-local constant = 500) → emit `converged(lastEnergy)` too (spec: capped sessions stop, cap ≠ error); `shouldStop` (engine stop flag) → exit cleanly. Define the threshold table as a file-local constexpr array of 8 doubles in Eh/bohr, in design D5's order crude…extreme: `{5e-3, 1e-3, 8e-4, 5e-4, 3e-4, 1e-4, 3e-5, 1e-6}` with a comment "approximate xtb optimizer level thresholds — tunable". Reset `LBfgs::resetHistory()` whenever the dragged atom index changes (task 3.5 wires that). Test slots: `waterConvergesToReferenceGeometry` (QSKIP when unavailable; water O at origin, H1 at (0,0,1.3 Å), H2 at (0, 0.1 Å, −0.95 Å), GFN2, level normal (index 4); pump `requestTick()` from a 30 ms QTimer in the test until `converged` OR 60 s timeout; assert O–H lengths in (0.86, 1.06) Å and angle in (94.5°, 114.5°), computing lengths from the last `coordsReady` payload converted to Å), `convergedStopsEvaluations` (after `converged`, record the `progress` evaluation counter, pump 20 more ticks, assert the counter did not increase). — Verify: build + `xvfb-run ctest -R xtbengine --output-on-failure` green (water convergence may take tens of seconds; that is acceptable for this test).

[OpenSpec 12] 3.5 Drag masking + pointer authority. Extend `XtbEngine`: member `m_draggedIndex` (−1 none) settable from any thread via mutex; `notifyDragPosition` stores the pointer-authored position for that atom (bohr). In the evaluate callback (task 3.4) when `m_draggedIndex >= 0`: overwrite that atom's 3 coordinates in the working array with the notified position BEFORE `updateMolecule`, and zero its 3 gradient entries AFTER `getGradient`; the atom's published coordinates therefore always equal the pointer position (spec coordinate write-back). On every change of `m_draggedIndex` (including −1→index and index→−1) call `LBfgs::resetHistory()`. Test slots: `draggedAtomPinnedDuringOptimization` (QSKIP when unavailable; setup water GFN2; start ticking; after ≥ 1 evaluation call `setDraggedAtom(1)` + `notifyDragPosition(1, {0.0, 0.0, 2.0/0.52917721092})` (≈2 Å along z in bohr) and keep ticking with fresh `notifyDragPosition` each tick; after ≥ 3 more evaluations read the last `coordsReady`, convert to Å, assert |H1 − (0,0,2.0)| < 1e-6 Å and that atom 0 and 2 coordinates CHANGED since the drag began — proving the rest relaxed while the dragged atom was pinned), `dragReleaseResumesCoverage` (continue the same flow: `setDraggedAtom(-1)`, pump ticks ≥ 3 evaluations, assert H1's coordinate is no longer exactly the pinned position). — Verify: build + `xvfb-run ctest -R xtbengine --output-on-failure` green.

[OpenSpec 13] 3.6 Interactive accuracy adaptation + threads env. Extend `XtbEngine::setup()` to FIRST apply the OpenMP environment via `qputenv` when the variable is unset: `OMP_WAIT_POLICY=PASSIVE` always; `OMP_NUM_THREADS` = `threadsSetting` if > 0 else auto (`qMax(1, qMin(8, QThread::idealThreadCount() - 1))`) — read-back with `qEnvironmentVariableIsSet` so a user's own env wins (design D7). Add public `void setInteractive(bool interactive)`; when interactive becomes true call `xtb_setAccuracy(env, calc, 0.2)` + `xtb_setMaxIter(env, calc, 30)` under the mutex; when false restore `1.0` / `100` — file-local constexpr `kXtbInteractiveAccuracy=0.2`, `kXtbInteractiveMaxIter=30`, `kXtbDefaultAccuracy=1.0`, `kXtbDefaultMaxIter=100` with a "tunable" comment. Reset L-BFGS history on each toggle (D6). ALSO call `setInteractive(true)`/`setInteractive(false)` automatically from the drag transitions of task 3.5. Test slots: `interactiveTogglesAccuracy` (QSKIP when unavailable; setup water; expose the applied accuracy by adding a getter `double currentAccuracy() const` on the engine; toggle and assert 0.2 then 1.0), `threadsEnvAutoRespectsClamp` (unset `OMP_NUM_THREADS` via `qunsetenv`, call `setup()` with 0, assert `qgetenv("OMP_NUM_THREADS").toInt()` is in [1,8]; then call setup with 3 and assert it equals 3; finally `qunsetenv("OMP_NUM_THREADS")` to not pollute other tests). — Verify: build + `xvfb-run ctest -R xtbengine --output-on-failure` green.

[OpenSpec 14] 3.7 GFN-FF parameter data locator (design D8). Create `libavogadro/src/xtb/xtbparams.h` + `libavogadro/src/xtb/xtbparams.cpp`, namespace `Avogadro::XtbParams`, one function: `bool ensureGfnffParameters(QString* diagnostic)` — logic: (1) if `XTBHOME` or `XTBPATH` is already set in the environment, return true untouched (respect user); (2) probe `QCoreApplication::applicationDirPath() + "/share/xtb"`; (3) probe `"/usr/share/xtb"`; a probe succeeds only if directory exists AND contains `.param_gfnff.xtb`; (4) on success `qputenv("XTBHOME", <dir>)` and `qputenv("XTBPATH", <dir>)` and return true; (5) on failure set a diagnostic naming the probed paths and return false. `XtbEngine::setup()` must call this BEFORE `xtb_loadGFNFF` when `method == 2`, and on false emit `setupFailed(diagnostic)` (once, clean up, return false — the spec's GFN-FF-without-data scenario). GFN1/GFN2 setups must NOT call the locator (no data files needed). Register the two files in the library sources like task 1.3. Test slots in `xtbenginetest.cpp`: `gfnffWaterSetupWhenParamsAvailable` (call `ensureGfnffParameters`; if false → `QSKIP("GFN-FF parameter data not available on this machine")`; else setup water method 2 → true), `gfnffWithoutParamsFailsDeterministically` (only runs when `ensureGfnffParameters` returns false — assert `setup()` returns false and `setupFailed` fired exactly once with a message mentioning "XTBHOME" or "param"; otherwise QSKIP). — Verify: build + `xvfb-run ctest -R xtbengine --output-on-failure` green (on this runner `/usr/share/xtb` is absent unless the `xtb` package is installed — both paths must pass).

[OpenSpec 15] 3.8 Quiesce safety. Extend `XtbEngine` teardown to the AutoOpt pattern: `stop()` sets the flag and wakes the wait condition; destructor runs `stop()`, then `wait()` (guarding `isRunning()`); the four xTB objects are deleted ONLY on the worker thread after its loop observed the stop flag and the current singlepoint returned — implement by having `run()` own deletion at exit and `setup()` only create; add a `bool m_quiesced` guard so `run()` deletes exactly once. Add a mutex rule comment: the GUI thread NEVER calls `xtb_del*` — it only calls `stop()` and `wait()`. Test slot: `immediateStopIsSafe` (QSKIP when unavailable; setup water, `start()`, call `stop()` within 1 ms (do not requestTick), `wait()` with a 10 s timeout asserting it returns true; then setup water again successfully — proving objects were rebuilt cleanly; repeat the whole cycle 5 times in one slot). — Verify: build + `xvfb-run ctest -R xtbengine --output-on-failure` green, then the full suite: `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` shows no new failures (this validates no state leaked into other tests).

[OpenSpec 16] 4.1 Engine selector UI + persistence. In `libavogadro/src/tools/autoopttool.cpp` `settingsWidget()`: add `QComboBox* m_comboEngine` (member in `autoopttool.h`) ABOVE the existing force-field combo, with entries in this order: "Force field", "xTB — GFN1-xTB", "xTB — GFN2-xTB", "xTB — GFN-FF" (constants `enum Engine { ForceField=0, Gfn1=1, Gfn2=2, GfnFf=3 };` in the header). When engine != ForceField: hide `m_comboFF` and `m_comboAlgorithm` (the FF-only controls) and show the xTB controls (add `QComboBox* m_comboLevel` with the 8 level names "Crude…Extreme", default index 4 = Normal, and reuse/keep the existing `m_stepsSpinBox`); when ForceField: the reverse. Persist via the tool's existing `writeSettings`/`readSettings` under keys `engine` and `xtbLevel`. Connect `currentIndexChanged` to a `void engineChanged()` slot doing the show/hide. MSVC-safe plain widgets only. Do NOT touch FF behavior yet. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target autoopttool -j8` succeeds and `xvfb-run ctest -R autooptrepro --output-on-failure` stays green.

[OpenSpec 17] 4.2 Availability gating. In `engineChanged()` and in `enable()`: when engine is an xTB entry and `!XtbApi::isAvailable()`, disable the Start button (`m_buttonStartStop->setEnabled(false)`), set its tooltip to "xTB library not found — force fields remain available", and emit the tool `message` signal with the same text (visible diagnostic — spec). When ForceField (or xTB with library present), restore enabled state. Do not change FF availability logic. — Verify: build target `autoopttool`; add a slot `xtbEngineGatedWithoutLibrary` to `libavogadro/tests/autooptreprotest.cpp` (follow that file's existing fixture pattern): construct the tool, read the settings widget, set engine combo to GFN2; if `!XtbApi::isAvailable()` assert the Start button `!isEnabled()`, else assert `isEnabled()`; `xvfb-run ctest -R autooptrepro --output-on-failure` green.

[OpenSpec 18] 4.3 Session routing. In `AutoOptTool::enable()`: branch on engine. ForceField path: exactly the existing code, unchanged. xTB path: collect `atomicNumbers` + `positionsAngstrom` from the molecule, call `m_xtbEngine->setup(numbers, positions, engineToMethod(engine), m_comboLevel->currentIndex(), m_threadsSpinBox ? m_threadsSpinBox->value() : 0)` (add member `XtbEngine* m_xtbEngine = nullptr;` created in the constructor, deleted in the destructor with `stop(); wait();` semantics per task 3.8 — the engine destructor handles it; do NOT delete while running). On setup failure show the failed-setup diagnostic in the HUD path (set a `m_setupFailed`-style flag already used by the FF path) and do not start. On success: `m_xtbEngine->start(QThread::LowPriority)`, start a `QBasicTimer` tick at 100 ms whose `timerEvent` calls `m_xtbEngine->requestTick()` and, if a `coordsReady` snapshot is pending (engine adds `bool takeLatestCoords(std::vector<double>& out)` returning false when nothing new, guarded by mutex), applies the snapshot to the molecule: molecule write lock (follow exactly how the FF path applies coordinates — same lock object and pattern), convert bohr→Å per atom index, `Atom::setPos`, then `Molecule::update()` + `GLWidget::update()`. Disable(): for xTB do `m_xtbEngine->stop()` then `quit()` is NOT needed (engine is not an event loop) — call `wait()` guarded by `isRunning()`, matching the engine's quiesce contract (3.8). Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-xtb-optimization" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-xtb-optimization" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Done when:

1. "openspec instructions apply --change add-xtb-optimization --json" reports zero remaining required implementation tasks.

2. Every explicit requirement and scenario in the active OpenSpec change has corresponding implementation evidence.

3. OpenSpec task completion accurately reflects the actual codebase state; no checkbox is marked complete merely because work was attempted.

4. Relevant builds, tests, and regression checks pass.

5. No known required work, implementation blocker, knowingly failing relevant test, or silently deferred required task remains.

6. A final comparison of the OpenSpec artifacts against the resulting implementation finds no substantive omission.

7. The repository is left in a coherent state suitable for subsequent OpenSpec verification/archive work.

8. Every mirrored GLLA task is complete (the GLLA task list shows no open tasks), so GLLA's pending-task gate does not refuse completion.

Do not declare the GLLA goal complete based only on previous conversation claims or task checkboxes. Verify against current repository and OpenSpec evidence.
